editorial.headline: Cereal Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers ready-to-eat, instant, and hot cereal products, with all business scales open and no Bali moratorium block recorded for PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10615 is a manufacturing classification for cereal foods. The record frames it around the making of ready-to-eat cereals, instant cereals, and hot cereal products, including rolled cereal, granola-style cereal, instant oatmeal, corn flakes, puffed grain, and muesli. It also includes cereal products made from soybeans and cereal-flour products made through extrusion. In plain English, this is the industrial home for businesses that turn grains, soy, or cereal flour into finished cereal foods rather than merely trading or packaging them.

The scale picture is broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the record does not reserve it for one size of company. A small producer making a focused cereal line and a larger manufacturer operating at industrial scale both sit inside the same activity description, provided the actual activity remains the manufacture of cereal foods described in the scope. That breadth matters because the code is not written as a niche craft category; it is an industrial food-processing category that can accommodate different operating scales.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The slim record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to the full stated ceiling. There is no separate minimum capital, licence timeline, tax treatment, or operational threshold in the record, so none should be assumed from this classification note alone.

The Bali picture is also clear, but it has to be stated carefully. The record does not mark this activity as blocked in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not caught by that block according to the record supplied. For a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the honest reading is therefore not a hidden Bali percentage or a local quota; it is simply that this cereal-manufacturing activity is nationally open and is not recorded here as blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
